newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa in hospital with heart problem.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa in hospital with heart problem.

text.p: Mother Teresa, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with the destitute, was taken to hospital with heart trouble on Friday, her doctor said.
It was the third time since August that the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun, who won the 1979 Nobel Peace prize, had been admitted to hospital for emergency care.

"She had some cardiac problems and we have decided to admit her," the doctor at Woodlands Nursing Home, in the eastern city of Calcutta, told Reuters. She was admitted at 2:30 a.m. (2100 GMT Thursday).
The doctor said the hospital would release a statement on her condition later in the day.
Sister Priscilla, a senior member of Mother Teresa's Missionaries of Charities religious order, said: "She had heart failure and chest pain and we had to remove her to hospital."
Mother Teresa spent nearly three weeks at Woodlands Nursing Home in late August and early September for heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia.
Two weeks after returning to her Calcutta-based order, she fell off a chair and hit her head. A brain scan revealed a blood clot in her brain but it disappeared and she was later released.
Mother Teresa's health began to deteriorate in 1989 when she was fitted with a heart pacemaker.
Since then she has spent time in hospital for heart disease, bacterial pneumonia, broken ribs, malaria, and lung problems.
Last Saturday, Mother Teresa received honorary American citizenship in a ceremony led by U.S. Ambassador to India Frank Wisner.

She is one of only five people to have received the accolade in America's 220 years as a nation. Others include former British prime minister Winston Churchill, Swedish diplomat Raoul Wallenberg and pioneer American settlers William and Hannah Penn.
Mother Teresa began her mission in the teeming slums of Calcutta and has inspired the world with her devotion to the poor.
Diminutive and bowed, her head shrouded by a sari, Mother Teresa has became a familiar symbol of commitment to the destitute and a living saint to her multitude of followers.

She began her task in 1949 in Calcutta, India's most densely populated city, and spread to open missions in 80 countries. Apart from poverty and hunger, she says, the world's major problems are loneliness and neglect.
Mother Teresa was born Agnes Goinxha Bejaxhiu to Albanian parents in Skopje, in what was then Serbia, on August 27, 1910.
At the age of 18 she became a Loretto nun, hoping to work at the Order's Calcutta mission.
She was sent to Loretto Abbey in Dublin and from there to India to begin her novitiate and teach geography at a convent school in Calcutta.
She said her divine call to work among the poor came in 1946. After training as a nurse with American missionaries, she opened her first Calcutta slum school in 1949.
